chapters.title: Chapter 6: Reporting and Getting It Right

lessons.title: Advance Tax on Capital Gains and Common Mistakes That Trigger Notices

body.text: Tax on a capital gain is due in the year you make it, in instalments, not when you file. The law gives you one generous concession for gains you could not have predicted, and charges 1% a month when you ignore it.

children.text: Anita, a 49-year-old college professor in Bhopal, sold a plot in November 2026 and calculated ₹3,00,000 of tax on the gain. She planned to pay it when filing her return in July 2027. That decision alone would have cost her ₹24,000 of interest. Paying by 15 December 2026 would have cost nothing.
Who Has to Pay Advance Tax

stats.label: Threshold
stats.context: Advance tax applies once your tax for the year, after TDS, reaches this

stats.label: Interest for shortfall
stats.context: Simple interest, charged on the unpaid amount

stats.label: Senior citizens
stats.context: Residents aged 60 and above with no business or professional income

children.text: Salaried employees usually never think about this, because their employer's TDS covers their salary tax. A capital gain changes that. Your broker deducts no TDS on share or fund sales, so the tax on those gains has to reach the government through advance tax instead.

markDefs.definition: A relief in the interest provision for deferment of advance tax: where income such as a capital gain arises after an instalment date, no interest is charged for earlier instalments if the tax on it is paid in the remaining instalments of the year, or by 31 March.

children.text: You cannot know in June that you will sell a flat in November, so the law does not expect you to. Under the

of the 1961 Act, if a capital gain arises after an instalment date, the earlier instalments are not treated as short, provided you pay the tax on that gain in the remaining instalments of the year, or by 31 March at the latest.

body.text: The concession removes interest for instalments that fell due before the gain arose. It does not let you postpone the tax to filing time. Miss the instalment that follows the sale, and interest starts running from there.

body.title: Interest Anita Pays on ₹3,00,000 of Tax, by When She Pays (Illustrative)
The Cost of Waiting to March
body.prompt: Anita's gain arose in November 2026 and the tax on it is ₹3,00,000. She skips the 15 December instalment and pays the whole amount on 15 March 2027. At 1% a month for three months on the shortfall, how much interest does she pay, in rupees?
body.explanation: ₹3,00,000 × 1% × 3 months = ₹9,000. The December instalment carries three months of interest. Paying on 15 December instead would have cost nothing, because the concession covers the June and September instalments for a November gain.

body.title: A February Sale
body.question: Rohit sells mutual fund units on 20 February 2027, creating tax of ₹80,000. By when must he pay it to avoid interest for deferment?
options: 15 December 2026, the instalment before the sale
15 March 2027, the next instalment after the sale
When he files his return in July 2027
body.explanation: The gain arose between 16 December and 15 March, so the tax on it belongs in the 15 March instalment. Pay it then and the earlier instalments are not treated as short. A gain arising after 15 March must be paid by 31 March.

body.title: Anita Waits Until Filing
body.scenario: Anita ignores both the December and March instalments and pays the full ₹3,00,000 only when she files her return in July 2027.
body.prompt: Roughly what does the delay cost, and what were her simpler options?
body.modelAnswer: She picks up interest for deferment on the December instalment of about ₹9,000, a further month on the March instalment of about ₹3,000, and interest for short payment of advance tax of roughly ₹12,000 for April to July, so about ₹24,000 in total on these illustrative numbers. Her simpler options were to pay ₹3,00,000 as advance tax by 15 December, or if she missed that, by 15 March to stop the larger charge. A salaried person can also ask their employer to deduct extra TDS from salary to cover other income, which spreads the payment without any instalment arithmetic.

body.text: Interest is calculated on the tax you should have paid, not on the gain. A large property or unlisted share sale can create a six-figure tax bill in one week, so work out the tax immediately after the sale rather than at filing time, and set that money aside.

body.title: What the Department Already Knows vs What People Report

columns.label: Reported to the Department
points: Every share and mutual fund sale, from brokers, depositories and registrars
Property registrations above the reporting threshold, from the sub-registrar
TDS on property purchases, dividends, crypto and interest
Large mutual fund purchases, cash deposits and credit card spends
Crypto trades reported by exchanges against your PAN

columns.label: Common Gaps in Returns
points: Gains left out because the money was reinvested or is still with the broker
ITR-1 filed when the taxpayer had gains or losses that need ITR-2
Exemption claimed without depositing unspent money in a capital gains account
Crypto shown as capital gains, or netted against losses
Foreign shares and RSUs missing from Schedule FA

body.title: The Letters You Might Receive, and What They Mean

children.text: Intimation after processing: the department processes your return and sends a computation. If its figures differ from yours, it shows a refund or a demand. Most mismatches at this stage are arithmetic or credit related, such as TDS not matching Form 26AS.
Defective return: the return is treated as incomplete, for example where a schedule is missing or the wrong form was used. You get time to correct it, and ignoring it can make the return invalid.

Assessment or reassessment notices: these follow when the department believes income has escaped tax, typically from third-party information such as a property registration or a large sale reported in the AIS.

Penalties: under-reporting of income attracts a penalty of 50% of the tax on that income, and deliberate misreporting 200%. Non-disclosure of foreign assets carries its own penalty under the Black Money Act, as Chapter 4 covered.

body.title: Where Mismatches Show Up First
body.textWithBlank: Before filing, compare your broker and fund statements against your ___, the statement showing what third parties have reported against your PAN.
body.explanation: Most notices to ordinary investors begin as a mismatch between the AIS and the return. Reconciling first, and submitting feedback where the AIS is wrong, prevents the majority of them.

body.label: Interest Rate on Late Tax
body.context: Charged as simple interest, and part of a month counts as a full month. It applies separately for deferment of instalments, short payment of advance tax and late filing, so the same delay can attract more than one charge.

cards.definition: Tax paid during the year itself, in four instalments, once your liability after TDS reaches ₹10,000.
No interest for instalments that fell due before the gain arose, if you pay in the next instalment or by 31 March.
Interest where advance tax paid is under 90% of the final tax, running from 1 April of the next year.
Interest for a short or missed instalment during the year.
Residents aged 60 and above with no business income need not pay advance tax.
A salaried taxpayer can ask the employer to deduct more tax to cover other income.

body.title: After Every Large Sale
steps: Work out the gain and the tax on it within a week of the sale
Identify which instalment date follows the sale and diarise it
Pay the tax on that gain by that instalment, or by 31 March for a late-March sale
Keep the challan; you will need the details when filing
Recheck your total advance tax against 90% of your expected final tax before 15 March
If you are salaried, consider asking your employer to deduct extra TDS instead

points: Advance tax applies once your tax after TDS reaches ₹10,000, in four instalments through the year
Brokers deduct no TDS on share and fund sales, so the tax on gains must be paid as advance tax
A gain arising after an instalment date carries no interest for earlier instalments if you pay by the next one, or 31 March
Interest runs at 1% a month and can apply under more than one provision for the same delay
The department already receives your trades, property registrations and TDS data, so unreported gains stand out
Reconciling with the AIS before filing prevents most notices sent to ordinary investors

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not tax or investment advice. Interest computations are simplified and illustrative; actual interest depends on exact dates, amounts and credits. Section numbers for interest and advance tax are given as they stand in the 1961 Act, and the corresponding numbering under the Income-tax Act, 2025 may differ. Consult a qualified tax professional before acting.
